label: D2 after choosing a1
explanation: Fires almost only at DELAY_2 on trials where the agent chose a1. At that step the last-action input is a1, so the choice is observed. It is essentially silent at D1 and GO. It fires on a1 trials whether the transition is common (S1) or rare (S2), but more often for S1 (72% vs 27% of D2 steps by state). Magnitude is highest after a run of consecutive a1 choices, typically while S1 is good and value is high. Activations are weak or absent on the first a1 choice after a run of a2 choices; these account for most false positives. Missed activations are small (1.7% of mass), at D2 on a2 trials, mostly rare S1 outcomes or a2 trials right after a1 runs. It does not fire on rewarded D1 inputs.

issues: Minor point: the claim that it is 'essentially silent at D1 and GO' holds. phase != D2 has mass recall 1.5e-5 on test, and GO and D1 each reach 0 coverage.

Misses are concentrated at D2 on a2 trials, as the explanation says (2.0% of mass on test; the (D2 & a2) predicate has precision 0.06). The examples are small activations, usually on a2 trials just after a1 runs or on rare S1 outcomes. They are a weak graded tail, not a separate class. Adding 'a2 after a1' to the predicate lowers F1 to 0.941.

The false positives (2804 of about 180k predicted on test) are mostly first a1 choices after a2 runs, as claimed. Even in that subset, precision is 0.90, so the feature mostly still fires there but weakly.
Common versus rare split of mass on D2 & a1: 78% when S1 is reached, 22% when S2 is reached. This matches 'fires on both, more on S1'.
Magnitude depends on the previous choice (D2 & a1 & previous a1 gives mass recall 0.74), which is consistent with the run-length claim. This is graded strength, not a gap in the predicate.
